Leave-one-out (cavity) Hosmer-Lemeshow test for penalised logistic regression

Source: R/cavity_gof.R
cavity.gof.Rd

Tests the fit of a ridge, lasso or elastic-net logistic regression in high dimensions, including \(p > n\). The textbook Hosmer-Lemeshow test groups on fitted probabilities that are shrunk and have seen their own responses, and after a penalised fit it rejects most correct models. This test groups, recalibrates and standardises on the leave-one-out linear predictor instead, computed from the one fit by a single Newton step, and refers the statistic to the familiar \(\chi^2_{G-2}\) law.

Usage

cavity.gof(
  X,
  y,
  lambda,
  alpha = 0,
  G = 10,
  lambda_scale = c("theory", "glmnet"),
  recalibration = c("auto", "logistic", "logistic-normal"),
  smooth.degree = 0,
  split = FALSE,
  reference = c("closed", "simulate"),
  B = 199,
  check.twins = TRUE,
  twin.cut = 0.999
)

Arguments

X

numeric matrix of predictors (no intercept column). Standardise the predictors before the call if wanted, not inside a procedure that uses all \(n\) observations to fit each one; the fit itself does not rescale them.

y

binary response (0/1).

lambda

penalty. On the theory scale (log-likelihood minus \(\lambda/2\) times the squared norm of the slopes; \(\lambda = n \lambda_{glmnet}\)) unless lambda_scale = "glmnet".

alpha

elastic-net mixing parameter: 0 (default) is the ridge, fitted internally; values in (0, 1] use glmnet (lasso at 1), and the leave-one-out index is computed on the active set.

G

number of groups (default 10).

lambda_scale

"theory" (default) or "glmnet".

recalibration

"auto" (logistic for \(n \le 5000\), logistic-normal above), "logistic" or "logistic-normal".

smooth.degree

degree of the smooth version (orthogonal polynomials in the group means of the index); 0 skips it.

split

if TRUE, also compute the sample-split test (index from a fit on the other half, so no approximation and no dependence between indices) and its cross-fitted version, which combines the two halves by the Cauchy combination.

reference

"closed" (default) or "simulate": refer \(S\) also to its distribution under the fitted model, by simulating responses from the fitted probabilities, refitting and recomputing \(S\), B times. Use it when twin.share is not near zero.

B

number of simulated data sets for reference = "simulate".

check.twins

if TRUE (default), compute the share of observations with a twin. It costs of order \(n^2\) times the size of the active set.

twin.cut

cosine above which two observations count as twins (default 0.999).

Value

An object of class "cavity.gof": a list with statistic (\(S\)), df, p.value (\(\chi^2_{G-2}\)), p.exact (the weighted chi-squared law of the grouped residuals), p.smooth, p.split, p.crossfit, p.simulated (when requested), twin.share, table (observed and expected counts and standardised residuals by group), recalibration (fitted intercept, slope and noise), index (the cavity index), beta, lambda, alpha.

Details

The reference law is derived for predictors that behave like independent draws. When many rows of X repeat, observations with the same row share the error of their index and the closed-form reference rejects too often; in a data set where half of the rows repeated, it rejected 57 per cent of correct models. The function then warns, and reference = "simulate" gives a reference conditional on the design.

References

Ebrahim, E. K. and Arashi, M. (2026). A leave-one-out goodness-of-fit test for penalised logistic regression in high dimensions. Submitted. Code archive: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23861454 .

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 300; p <- 60
X <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n)
y <- rbinom(n, 1, 1 / (1 + exp(-drop(X %*% rnorm(p, sd = 0.3)))))
res <- cavity.gof(X, y, lambda = 50)
res
#> 
#> Leave-one-out (cavity) Hosmer-Lemeshow test
#>   fit: ridge, lambda = 50 (theory scale), n = 300, active predictors = 60
#>   recalibration: logistic, slope = 1.531
#>   S = 8.794 on 8 df:  P = 0.36  (exact weighted law: P = 0.3626)
#>   share of observations with a twin: 0.000
